storyboard.addedInformation: Names the mechanism: a mistuned broadcast, not low intelligence.
storyboard.claim: Feeling surrounded by idiots means broadcasting on the wrong frequency.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker mid-sentence, unheard, beside the colleague who has already switched off — a broadcast nobody is tuned to.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open.

storyboard.addedInformation: The mirror makes the blind spot visible: the viewer sees himself as the measure.
storyboard.claim: Everyone assumes their own brain is the objective default.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mirror: the worker studies his own reflection as the baseline for normal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the mistuned broadcast to why it happens: we treat our own mind as standard.

storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the psychology term a face: the author names the bias directly.
storyboard.claim: Psychology names this blind spot the false consensus effect.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Thomas Erikson pointing as he labels the bias for the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the blind spot from the previous beat.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the belief as a spoken conviction, not an abstract idea.
storyboard.claim: We believe our values, pace, and style are simply normal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker insisting his own pace and style are just how things are done.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Spells out what the false consensus effect claims.

storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing finger shows the verdict: difference gets sentenced, not studied.
storyboard.claim: Any deviation from our normal reads as total incompetence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart jabbing a finger in judgment at staff who work differently.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the belief to its verdict on everyone else.

storyboard.addedInformation: The strike visibly cancels the incompetence verdict the last beat delivered.
storyboard.claim: It is not incompetence; it is a translation issue behind every conflict.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson rejecting the incompetence label: the phrase itself crossed out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Overturns the previous beat's verdict.

storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the abstraction in the dishwasher standoff the hosts name.
storyboard.claim: Boardroom fights and dishwasher standoffs are color collisions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The four-color grid over a tense kitchen standoff about loading the dishwasher.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rejected label to the replacement: colliding colors.

storyboard.addedInformation: The accusing tone shows the judging the narration describes.
storyboard.claim: We speak our native behavior and judge others for not getting it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker berating a colleague who simply operates on another wavelength.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the collision to how we cause it: judging instead of translating.

storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the promised payoff on the case that proves the stakes: Stuart.
storyboard.claim: Translate the message and the idiots disappear; Stuart shows the stakes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart looming as the case subject: get this wrong and this is your future.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the method to its payoff and the warning case.

storyboard.addedInformation: The briefcase marks decades of genuinely built business success.
storyboard.claim: Stuart was a capable entrepreneur who built a successful firm.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart holding his briefcase: the self-made boss at the height of success.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the man behind the warning.

storyboard.addedInformation: The sweeping gesture condemns every department at once, as he did.
storyboard.claim: He believed every department was staffed by complete morons.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart sweeping a hand across the office: all of them, morons.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From his success to his diagnosis of everyone else.

storyboard.addedInformation: The open-mouth tirade shows he broadcast the verdict, never softened it.
storyboard.claim: He openly branded department A hopeless blockheads.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart shouting the verdict aloud, no inhibition.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The diagnosis gets its first target.

storyboard.addedInformation: The factory-floor pointing shows public shaming, not private grumbling.
storyboard.claim: Department B were total fools, dressed down on the factory floor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart dressing down staff in the open, finger leveled at them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From department A to department B: no one is spared.

storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows survival mode under a toxic, abrasive regime.
storyboard.claim: The toxic climate forced staff into covert survival operations.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cowed employee shrinking under the public tirades, plotting how to survive Tuesday.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the boss's attack to its effect on staff.

storyboard.addedInformation: The scheming look sells the desperate ingenuity the hosts admire.
storyboard.claim: Their desperate answer was a brilliant piece of corporate espionage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The employee scheming the secret warning system.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the need to hide to the desperate plan.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the artifact itself: the discreet bulb above reception.
storyboard.claim: Staff installed a secret warning bulb above reception.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The small signal lamp above the office door, installed in secret.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the plan to the device.

storyboard.addedInformation: Red pairs the lamp with the approaching threat: Stuart is in the building.
storyboard.claim: Stuart inside meant the receptionist switched the lamp to red.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart storming in beneath the glowing red door lamp.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lamp's red meaning: the boss is here.

storyboard.addedInformation: The hesitant pause before the double doors shows the checking ritual.
storyboard.claim: Staff and vendors checked the lamp before entering the doors.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A visitor hesitating at the double doors, eyes on the signal lamp.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From what red means to who reads it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The retreat walk shows red light meant flight, not courage.
storyboard.claim: On red, people fled to their cars rather than face the founder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A visitor turning on his heels and walking back out to escape Stuart.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Red light consequences: the retreat.

storyboard.addedInformation: The puzzling-over pose pivots from anecdote to analysis.
storyboard.claim: The fascinating question is the mechanism behind Stuart's hostility.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson pausing to dissect what drove Stuart's behavior.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the crazy symptom to its cause.

storyboard.addedInformation: The briefcase and steady stance show competence, contradicting the evil reading.
storyboard.claim: He was not evil, just a highly proficient, driven businessman.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart composed with his briefcase: formidable, not villainous.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the monster as a mistranslator.

storyboard.addedInformation: The mirror shows he measured everyone against his own reflection.
storyboard.claim: His failure: no translation skills, his own baseline as the standard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart studying his own reflection as the measure of all capability.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the exact failure behind the hostility.

storyboard.addedInformation: The jab shows slower or softer workers stamped defective on the spot.
storyboard.claim: Anyone slower or less ruthless was categorized as defective.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart condemning a colleague who processes data at another speed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the private standard to the public sentence.

storyboard.addedInformation: The shouting pose is the FM man screaming at AM receivers.
storyboard.claim: Stuart screamed like an FM radio at a world of AM radios.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart shouting at colleagues tuned to a different frequency.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The case compressed into one image.

storyboard.addedInformation: Places the physical book in the author's hands as the framework source.
storyboard.claim: Today's framework comes from Thomas Erikson's Surrounded by Idiots.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson presenting the book itself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the parable to the book that explains it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The grid is the matrix being built; the pointing hand commits to it.
storyboard.claim: Do not become Stuart: today we build a translation matrix.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The four-color grid the viewer will construct, chosen, not feared.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the book to the mission: build the matrix.

storyboard.addedInformation: The grid appears before any color is assigned, matching the order taught.
storyboard.claim: First understand the grid of behavior before assigning any colors.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson indicating the blank behavior grid and its defining axes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The matrix work begins with the underlying grid.

storyboard.addedInformation: The dinner plate grounds the thought experiment everyone has lived.
storyboard.claim: Picture the scene we all know: a crowded dinner party, long table.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dinner table set with plates: the familiar party scene.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From theory to the scene that will teach it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The loud open-mouth delivery is the volume turned all the way up.
storyboard.claim: On your right, one guest takes over, loud and categorical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The loud guest dominating the table, holding court mid-declaration.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The camera finds the loud end of the table.

storyboard.addedInformation: The smug grin exposes confidence built on almost nothing.
storyboard.claim: His ironclad geopolitical thesis rests on one half-watched documentary.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The guest's self-satisfied certainty despite the thin source.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boast deflates: the source is paper-thin.

storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk holds the room's acoustic space without a flicker of doubt.
storyboard.claim: Zero hesitation: he occupies all the acoustic space, then we look away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: One guest filling the whole room and the quiet guest at the far end of the table — the contrast the narration turns on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Certainty peaks, then the gaze shifts down the table.

storyboard.addedInformation: The quiet motion contrasts the shouting: service without a speech.
storyboard.claim: At the far end, a guest of a dozen words silently clears the plates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The quiet guest up and moving, gathering empty appetizer plates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Hard cut from the loudest guest to the quietest.

storyboard.addedInformation: The cup in hand shows the unasked hospitality: refills and fresh decaf.
storyboard.claim: Unasked, they refill glasses and brew a fresh pot of decaf.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The quiet guest serving drinks, cup in hand, nobody having asked.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The quiet service continues.

storyboard.addedInformation: The reaching hand meets needs before they are voiced.
storyboard.claim: They instinctively monitor and quietly meet the group's needs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The guest reaching to tend the table, reading needs before words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the acts of service to the instinct behind them.

storyboard.addedInformation: The two buckets sort the whole party into the system's raw material.
storyboard.claim: That dinner contrast illustrates the two intersecting axes of behavior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two buckets: the loud guest versus the quiet guest, side by side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The scene collapses into its structural lesson.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names the lineage: early twentieth-century theory behind the axes.
storyboard.claim: The axes trace back to Carl Jung and William Marston.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson tracing the system to its founders, Jung and Marston.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the axes to their origin story.

storyboard.addedInformation: The paperwork is the DISC assessment and pressure-test research.
storyboard.claim: Marston built the DISC assessment and the test behind the polygraph.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Assessment notes and pressure-test papers: behavior measured on paper.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the man to his measurements.

storyboard.addedInformation: The comic book in the surprised delivery lands the trivia twist.
storyboard.claim: The same Marston created Wonder Woman.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Wonder Woman comic book: the personality theorist's other creation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the laboratory to the comic-book twist.

storyboard.addedInformation: The steady explainer tone carries the obsession with truth and feeling.
storyboard.claim: Marston was obsessed with emotional response and truth in behavior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson explaining the obsession that drove Marston's work.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the trivia back to what Marston was chasing.

storyboard.addedInformation: The grid returns as behavior stops looking like noise.
storyboard.claim: Behavior is not noise; it runs on a predictable grid, starting with focus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The behavior grid resolving out of chaos: task versus people comes first.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The history lands on the payoff: a lawful grid.
